messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Help with a BIogeobears scenario
parts:
Hi- a key issue is to be clear on what the parameters mean. 

Eg “d” is the rate of range-expansion dispersal, not the “range”.

The “j” parameter is the relative weight of jump dispersal - discussed in detail on PhyloWiki (google it)

Both “d” and “j” events can be short-distance or long-distance dispersal, it depends only on the distance between areas. Although, to make a gross generalization, probably j events are more often long-distance events than d-events.

To actually measure the effect of geographic distance on dispersal, use a +x model variant, see eg Van Dam and Matzke 2016, J Biogeographic.

To actually get a probabilistic sample of possible exact dispersal histories, which you could manually classify into short or long distance based on a distance cutoff, use Biogeographic Stochastic Mapping, see Dupin, Matzke et al 2017, J Biogeog.

Cheers,
Nick

On Sunday, December 15, 2019, Adam Rick Bessa <adamri...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi everyone,

I would like to ask everyone's help to understand a scenario.
I have a biogeographic scenario in which the groups with reduced genetic divergence are separated by the Andes.

Biogeobears analysis indicated two models as the best fit to our data (DEC + J and DIVALIKE + J), with DIVALIKE + J being the best supported model (attached). Estimates of parameters d (dispersal range), e (extinction) and j founder-event show a greater support tendency for parameter j (founder-event or jump-dispersal). However, my other analysis (ABC and IMa) show clear support for a long-dispersal distance scenario, which would be at odds with Biogeobears-supported jump-dispersal (j).

The distribution of probabilities for the parameters d (range dispersal), e (extinction) and  (founder-event) indicate that the analysis was difficult to recover the long-distance dispersal recovered by other analysis (ABC and IMa)? 

If this is true, what could explain this contradiction of Biogeobears with ABC and IMa? Is there any technical question for this?

Just to help the debate. The group studied occurs from South America to Central America. However, I do not have a representative sampling of species distribution, mainly near the mountain range where, which is somewhat vicarious for this group. Is there any relationship of incomplete sampling of species in the Biogeobears analysis?



Thank you for your contribution,


Best,

Adam Bessa
